prompt: What does an account have to do to get Shield Standard?
hint: Look at the bill and the console.

choices.text: Subscribe to it for a year
choices.why: That is Shield Advanced.

choices.text: Nothing; every account has it
choices.why: Right. It is on, free, with nothing to configure.

choices.text: Attach a web ACL to every load balancer
choices.why: A web ACL is WAF, a separate service.

choices.text: Enable it in each region
choices.why: There is no setting for it.

prompt: A flood of well-formed GET /search requests is slowing the shop. Which protection is built for it?

choices.text: Shield Standard, which absorbs floods
choices.why: Standard does not read HTTP; these requests look ordinary at layer 4.

choices.text: A larger instance type
choices.why: It answers more of the flood and stops none of it.

choices.text: A security group rule
choices.why: Security groups filter by address and port, not by request.

choices.text: A WAF rate-based rule on the /search path
choices.why: Right. And CloudFront in front to cache what can be cached.

prompt: Match each attack to the layer it works at.

pairs.left: Thousands of login attempts a second

prompt: What is Shield Advanced's cost protection?

choices.text: A cap that stops the bill from growing during an attack
choices.why: Nothing stops the bill; the credit comes afterwards.

choices.text: A refund of the subscription if no attack happens
choices.why: The subscription is paid either way.

choices.text: A credit, after the attack, for its scaling
choices.why: Right. On resources protected at the time.

choices.text: Free data transfer out for protected resources
choices.why: Protected resources pay an extra data transfer line.

prompt: What must an account have before the Shield Response Team can help it?

choices.text: A Business or Enterprise support plan
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A web ACL attached to every protected resource
choices.why: Useful, but not the requirement.

choices.text: A dedicated AWS account for security
choices.why: Not a requirement for the response team.

choices.text: Proactive engagement switched off
choices.why: Proactive engagement is something the team can add, not a precondition.

prompt: During an HTTP flood, what does Shield Advanced's automatic application-layer mitigation do?

choices.text: Doubles the load balancer's capacity for the attack
choices.why: Capacity is the application's; Shield writes rules.

choices.text: Writes WAF rules into the resource's web ACL, then removes them
choices.why: Right. Rules aimed at the attack, gone when it ends.

choices.text: Moves the site behind CloudFront
choices.why: It changes no architecture.

choices.text: Blocks every address outside Brazil
choices.why: It targets the attack's signature, not a country.

prompt: On a real account, what does aws shield create-subscription commit to?
hint: The lab's warning, before the command.

choices.text: A free trial for 30 days
choices.why: There is no trial.

choices.text: A one-off fee of 3,000 USD
choices.why: It is monthly, for twelve months.

choices.text: Nothing until a resource is protected
choices.why: The subscription is charged from the moment it exists.

choices.text: 3,000 USD a month for a year
choices.why: Right. And it cannot be cancelled within the year.

prompt: The subscription's TimeCommitmentInSeconds is 31536000. How many days is that?
A team regrets its Shield Advanced subscription in month three. What can it change?

choices.text: Delete it, paying a fee
choices.why: It cannot be cancelled during its year, with or without a fee.

choices.text: Move it to another region
choices.why: It is not regional; it belongs to the organisation.

choices.text: Turn off auto-renew
choices.why: Right. update-subscription --auto-renew DISABLED.

choices.text: Delete its protections to stop the monthly fee
choices.why: That stops the data transfer line, not the fee.

prompt: moto accepted create-protection before any subscription existed. What does AWS do?

choices.text: Refuses it
choices.why: Right. A protection belongs to a Shield Advanced subscription.

choices.text: Accepts it as Shield Standard
choices.why: Standard has no protections to create.

choices.text: Creates the subscription automatically
choices.why: Nothing commits an account to a year implicitly.

choices.text: Accepts it and bills it per day
choices.why: There is no daily protection price.

prompt: A protected load balancer sends 3 TB (3,000 GB) in a month. What is the Shield data transfer line, in USD?
Over the year of commitment, what does the shop's Shield Advanced cost, at 3,100 USD a month?
An organisation has 30 accounts paying through one bill. How many 3,000 USD subscriptions does it pay?

choices.text: 30, one per account
choices.why: Additional subscriptions are 0 USD.

choices.text: One; the others are free
choices.why: Right. $0 for additional subscriptions.

choices.text: One per region the accounts use
choices.why: The subscription is not regional.

choices.text: Thirty, at a volume discount
choices.why: There is no such discount line.

prompt: A shop sells 24,000 USD a day, evenly. How many hours of downtime equal the 37,200 USD of a year's subscription?
Which team gains least from buying Shield Advanced now?
hint: The subscription speeds up layer 7 work that must already exist.

choices.text: A payments platform losing 50,000 USD an hour down
choices.why: One hour pays more than a year's subscription.

choices.text: A service that auto-scales hard under load
choices.why: Cost protection is built for exactly that.

choices.text: A company whose contracts require DDoS response
choices.why: A contractual requirement is a reason to buy.

choices.text: A team that has never read its WAF logs
choices.why: Right. It will spend the attack learning its own traffic.
